principle.name: Idempotency First
principle.description: Every script and operation must be safe to run multiple times without causing unintended side effects or errors.
principle.rationale: Users should be able to re-run setup scripts to ensure their environment is in the correct state without fear of breaking things.

example.good: # Check before installing if ! command -v ripgrep &>/dev/null; then brew install ripgrep fi
example.bad: # Always tries to install, may error if already present brew install ripgrep

principle.name: Zero Trust Security
principle.description: Never trust input, environment variables, or external dependencies without validation. Assume everything can be compromised.
principle.rationale: Scripts run with user privileges and can cause significant damage if exploited. Defense in depth prevents security breaches.

example.good: # Validate and sanitize path readonly INSTALL_DIR="${HOME}/.local/bin" if [[ ! "$INSTALL_DIR" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_./-]+$ ]]; then log_error "Invalid installation directory" exit 1 fi mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR"
example.bad: # Blindly trusting user input mkdir -p $INSTALL_DIR # Unquoted, vulnerable to injection

principle.name: Explicit Over Implicit
principle.description: Make all behaviors explicit. Avoid hidden defaults or assumptions about the environment.
principle.rationale: Cross-platform scripts fail when they assume specific behaviors. Being explicit ensures consistent behavior across platforms.

principle.name: Graceful Degradation
principle.description: When optional dependencies are unavailable, continue with reduced functionality rather than failing completely.
principle.rationale: Different platforms have different available tools. Scripts should work as well as possible given the available resources.

example.good: # Check terminal capability if [[ -t 1 ]] && command -v tput &>/dev/null; then RED=$(tput setaf 1) NC=$(tput sgr0) else RED="" NC="" fi echo "${RED}Error${NC}: Something went wrong"
example.bad: # Assumes ANSI colors always work echo -e "\033[0;31mError\033[0m: Something went wrong"

convention.rule: Use readonly for constants and declare local variables explicitly

examples.good:
readonly VERSION="1.0.0" readonly CONFIG_DIR="${HOME}/.config/myapp"
my_function() { local input="$1" local result="" # ... }

convention.rule: Always quote variables unless word splitting is intentional

examples.good: file_path="$HOME/my file.txt" if [[ -f "$file_path" ]]; then cat "$file_path" fi
examples.bad: file_path=$HOME/my file.txt # Will fail if [ -f $file_path ]; then # Will fail with spaces cat $file_path fi

convention.rule: Use [[ ]] for conditionals in Bash, [ ] for POSIX sh

examples.good:
# Bash script if [[ -n "$var" && "$var" == "value" ]]; then echo "Match" fi
# POSIX sh script if [ -n "$var" ] && [ "$var" = "value" ]; then echo "Match" fi
examples.bad: # Mixing styles or using == in [ ] if [ -n $var ] && [ $var == "value" ]; then echo "Match" fi

convention.rule: Use trap for cleanup and handle errors at every step

examples.bad: #!/bin/bash TEMP_FILE=$(mktemp) # Work with temp file... rm -f "$TEMP_FILE" # May not run if script exits early

convention.rule: Use descriptive function names and document parameters

examples.good: # Install a package using the appropriate package manager # Arguments: # $1 - Package name # Returns: # 0 on success, 1 on failure install_package() { local package="${1:?Package name required}" # Implementation... }

pitfall.why_problematic: Backticks don't nest well and are harder to read
ls output is locale-dependent and breaks on special characters
pitfall.correct_approach:
# Use globs or find instead for file in "$dir"/*; do [[ -f "$file" ]] && process "$file" done
# Or with find find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -exec process {} \;

pitfall.why_problematic: In Bash, empty arrays with set -u cause unbound variable errors
pitfall.correct_approach:
# Use array length check if [[ ${#my_array[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then for item in "${my_array[@]}"; do echo "$item" done fi
# Or use ${array[@]+"${array[@]}"} pattern for item in ${my_array[@]+"${my_array[@]}"}; do echo "$item" done

pitfall.why_problematic: In some environments (cron, minimal containers) HOME may not be set
pitfall.correct_approach:
# Provide fallback readonly HOME_DIR="${HOME:-$(getent passwd "$(id -un)" | cut -d: -f6)}"
# Or fail explicitly if [[ -z "${HOME:-}" ]]; then log_error "HOME environment variable not set" exit 1 fi
